domain: Social Ontology / Identity Politics / Legal Classification
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested category kernel governing membership in sex/gender classes. Two primary readings instantiate structurally different constraints: sex-as-biology grounds membership in immutable reproductive anatomy, while gender-as-identity grounds membership in subjective self-identification. Each reading produces different victim sets, different authority structures for adjudication, and different extractiveness profiles.

key_entities: Trans women (individuals assigned male at birth identifying as women)
Cis women (individuals assigned female at birth identifying as women)
Medical/legal gatekeepers (authority structures for category adjudication)
key_tensions: Immutable biological criteria vs mutable identity criteria for category membership
Trans inclusion vs cis women's safety/fairness claims in single-sex spaces
Self-ID authority vs institutional gatekeeping authority
key_mechanisms: Legal recognition systems (birth certificate amendment, gender marker change)
Institutional access control (who adjudicates entry to sex-segregated spaces)
key_absences: Intersex individuals (neither reading cleanly accommodates non-binary biology)
Non-Western gender systems (two-spirit, hijra, fa'afafine traditions absent from both readings)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The shared commitment is that humans can be categorized into sex/gender classes with differential rights, protections, and access to spaces. Both readings accept this substrate but disagree on what grounds membership.
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Biology reading: medical/scientific authority via chromosomal/anatomical observation. Identity reading: individual autonomy via self-declaration, sometimes mediated by psychological diagnosis.

readings.commitment: Category membership determined by immutable reproductive biology (chromosomes, anatomy at birth)
readings.authority_grounding: Medical/scientific observation; chromosomal testing as final arbiter
readings.expected_structural_delta: Trans women excluded from 'woman' category; cis women are sole victim set for sex-based harms; high boundary enforcement costs; intersex individuals forced into binary

readings.commitment: Category membership determined by subjective gender identity (self-identification)
readings.authority_grounding: Individual autonomy; psychological self-knowledge as primary evidence
readings.expected_structural_delta: Trans women included in 'woman' category; victim set expands to include trans women experiencing misogyny; cis women lose exclusive claim to sex-based protections; low boundary enforcement costs but high conflict over space access

readings.commitment: Category membership determined by combination of biology and social transition (medical gatekeeping model)
readings.authority_grounding: Medical/psychiatric authority via diagnosis and treatment protocols
readings.expected_structural_delta: Trans women conditionally included after medical transition; victim set partially overlaps; high gatekeeping costs; authority concentrated in medical institutions; excludes non-transitioning trans individuals

axes.structural_delta: Category membership grounded in chromosomal/anatomical sex assigned at birth; immutable boundary
axes.primary_observable: Chromosomal karyotype (XX/XY); primary/secondary sex characteristics at birth; legal birth certificate sex marker under biology-reading jurisdictions
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; highest extractiveness; clearest victim set

axes.structural_delta: Category membership grounded in individual's subjective gender identity; mutable boundary via self-declaration
axes.primary_observable: Self-reported gender identity; legal gender marker in self-ID jurisdictions; institutional policies allowing self-declaration
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; structurally opposite victim set from biology_reading

axes.structural_delta: Category membership grounded in medical diagnosis and treatment; conditional boundary via institutional authority
axes.primary_observable: Gender dysphoria diagnosis rates; hormone therapy/surgery completion; legal systems requiring medical evidence for gender marker change
axes.selection_reason: Third reading; reveals authority structure as independent constraint; highest institutional extraction

axes.human_readable: Single-Sex Space Access Control (Institutional Boundary Enforcement)
axes.structural_delta: Mechanism for adjudicating entry to sex-segregated spaces (prisons, sports, shelters); enforcement varies by which reading institutions adopt
axes.primary_observable: Institutional policies on trans inclusion in single-sex spaces; litigation rates over access disputes; violence/safety incident rates in contested spaces
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream application of kernel readings; captured by reading-level analysis

axes.human_readable: Intersex Exclusion (Binary Enforcement on Non-Binary Biology)
axes.structural_delta: Neither biology nor identity reading accommodates individuals with DSDs (differences of sex development); forced binary assignment
axes.primary_observable: Intersex infant surgery rates; legal recognition of non-binary sex markers; intersex advocacy group positions on sex/gender frameworks
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: important absence but structurally upstream; omega material for kernel coherence boundary

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Institutional boundary enforcement for sex-segregated spaces
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream application mechanism; captured by reading-level constraint stories
Structurally upstream absence; omega material for kernel coherence test

omegas.description: Does the existence of intersex individuals (1.7% of population with DSDs) falsify the kernel itself? If biology is not cleanly binary, the biology_reading collapses. If identity is self-determined but intersex individuals are surgically assigned, the identity_reading's autonomy claim is undermined. The kernel may be a false binary imposed on non-binary substrate.
omegas.source: Deferred axis intersex_exclusion + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Two-spirit, hijra, fa'afafine, and other non-Western gender systems are absent from both readings. Are these third categories (falsifying the binary kernel) or cultural variations on the same binary (preserving the kernel)? If third categories, the kernel is Western-specific, not universal.
omegas.source: Extraction absence + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Each reading claims a victim set: biology_reading claims cis women are victimized by trans inclusion; identity_reading claims trans women are victimized by exclusion. Are these symmetrical (both readings equally extractive) or asymmetrical (one reading's victims face greater harm)? Observable: comparative harm metrics (violence rates, suicide rates, discrimination measures) across victim sets.

The hybrid_reading concentrates authority in medical gatekeepers, but if gender dysphoria is depathologized (as homosexuality was), the medical authority grounding collapses. Is hybrid_reading a stable reading or a transitional state between biology and identity readings?

Sports competition is the highest-salience single-sex space dispute. Does biology_reading preserve fairness (via testosterone/muscle mass differences) or does identity_reading preserve inclusion (via anti-discrimination norms)? Observable: performance data for trans athletes vs cis athletes in same category. This may be the empirical test case for which reading better satisfies the kernel's purpose.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure confirmed: three readings emit structurally distinct constraints with non-overlapping victim sets. Intersex exclusion and non-Western systems are genuine absences that test kernel coherence but do not invalidate the reading decomposition. Victim set symmetry (omega_victim_set_symmetry) is the primary empirical uncertainty.
